issues.description: The declaration of ray_sphere_intersect in the template header omits the radius parameter, but the implementation defines ray_sphere_intersect with a radius parameter. The solution header declares the function with the radius parameter. This header/implementation mismatch in the template will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the correct function signature to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the function declaration in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h of the template to include the radius parameter so it matches the implementation and the solution. For example: bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); Then recompile to ensure the header and implementation signatures are consistent.

issues.description: The function ray_sphere_intersect is declared with different signatures across artifacts: the template header (example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h) declares ray_sphere_intersect(origin, dir, center) without a radius parameter, while the template implementation (example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.cpp) and the solution header (example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h) include an additional radius parameter (origin, dir, center, radius). This mismatch makes it unclear which interface students should implement/use, can cause compilation/link errors, and forces students to reconcile inconsistent interfaces instead of focusing on the algorithm.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the declaration in example_program/src/ray_sphere_intersect.h consistent with the implementation and solution by adding the radius parameter: bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); Ensure both template and solution headers match the implementation to avoid confusion and compilation issues.
